LED1 prüfen: GPIO17 → B1\n\n1. Raspi her:
Test LED1: GPIO17 → B1

1. Shut down the Pi and disconnect all power sources.
2. J7: bridge the upper two pins (manual Fig. 7).
3. Connect J2 “GP17” to J3 “B1” with a wire.
4. Bridge the “B1 out” pair above U3; leave “B1 in” open.
5. Start. App: GPIO17, Output (starts LOW), Activate pin.
6. HIGH: LED D1 on. LOW: LED D1 off. Do not press S1 during this test.

If D1 stays off: release the pin, disconnect power and check J7, the wire and the OUT jumper.
A HIGH reading in the app confirms only the level at the Pi.
Taster S1 prüfen: GPIO17 → B1\n\n1. Pin:
Test button S1: GPIO17 → B1

1. Release the pin, shut down the Pi and disconnect all power sources.
2. Keep the GP17 → B1 wire; leave both B1 IN/OUT jumper pairs open.
   Set J7 as for the LED test.
3. Start. App: GPIO17, Input, Pull-Up, Activate pin.
4. S1 released: HIGH. Hold S1 down for 2 seconds: LOW.

Without an OUT bridge, LED D1 may stay on independently of the app reading.
To make D1 follow: with power disconnected, bridge only the B1 OUT pair above U3 using a jumper cap or an F-F lead; leave B1 IN open.
GPIO17 remains an input with pull-up. Released: D1 on; pressed: D1 off.

Use GPIO17 here; the old GP0/GP1 have fixed pull-ups.
The app cannot detect jumpers or wiring automatically.
